conventions.convention: T(S) is the algebraic direct sum of algebraic tensor powers of complex Schwartz space on R⁴; multiplication concatenates factors, and involution reverses their order and conjugates them. Degree zero is C with unit 1.
Distribution pairings are bilinear. W₀ = 1, each Wₙ is continuous on Schwartz space on R⁴ⁿ, and positivity means ω(a* a) is real and nonnegative for every algebra element a.

The Hilbert inner product is linear in its first variable. A weak operator-valued tempered distribution is a complex-linear map S → Lin(D), preserving one dense domain D, with continuous scalar coefficients for every pair of vectors in D.
The Minkowski signature is (+,−,−,−); gx = Λx + a and T_g f(x) = f(g⁻¹x). The group has the matrix-subspace/product topology. The closed forward cone is p⁰ ≥ |p⃗|.

Assuming Countable Choice, F_M ψ(z) = ∫ exp(−i p·z) ψ(p) d⁴p; distributional Fourier transformation is bilinear transposition. Support in a closed set means vanishing on compact smooth tests supported outside it.
The Yukawa comparison uses μ ≥ 0, r = |x| > 0 and Δ = ∂₁² + ∂₂² + ∂₃²; it concerns only pointwise equations away from the origin.

load_bearing.statement: A positive tempered moment family consists of W₀ = 1 and continuous complex-linear Wₙ on Sₙ whose evaluations on product tests extend to a normalized positive complex-linear functional ω on T(S).

For every g in the proper-orthochronous Poincaré group, T_g maps S continuously to itself; for each fixed f in S, g ↦ T_g f is continuous. The induced tensor action consists of unital star-automorphisms and obeys α_g α_h = α_gh.
A weak operator-valued tempered distribution on a dense common domain D is a complex-linear map Φ: S → Lin(D) such that f ↦ (Φ(f)u,v) is a continuous complex-linear functional for every u,v in D.

Assuming Countable Choice, define the Minkowski Fourier transform of a tempered distribution D by ⟨D̂_M,ψ⟩ = ⟨D,F_M ψ⟩, with F_M ψ(z) = ∫ exp(−i p·z) ψ(p) d⁴p; support in C means vanishing on every compact smooth test supported disjointly from C.

published_dependencies.used_for: Defines the test spaces and product-test, affine-pullback seminorm estimates.
Defines continuity and convergence through finite seminorm neighborhoods.
Defines continuous complex-linear Schwartz functionals and bilinear pairings.
Defines the complete inner-product target of the common-domain weak field.
Fixes the first-variable-linear complex inner-product convention.
States the explicit choice assumption carried by Hilbert completion and Fourier suppliers.
Supplies the Countable-Choice Hilbert completion used by the qft-mc01 GNS prerequisite.
Supplies the Euclidean 2π normalization and bilinear-transposition convention.
Establishes the Schwartz Fourier automorphism under Countable Choice.
Justifies output composition with z ↦ ηz/(2π) in the Minkowski Fourier definition.
Supplies compact-support terminology cited by the Fourier-support convention.
Defines complex compactly supported smooth tests used in the locality conclusion.
Justifies viewing compact smooth tests as Schwartz tests.
Makes bounded continuous translation coefficients regular tempered distributions.

concerns.concern: The Fewster–Rejzner reference locator says “PDF pp. 10–11, equations (12) and (14)”. In the linked arXiv v2 PDF, equation (12) and the r⁻² Yukawa expression occur on PDF/printed page 11, while equation (14) occurs on page 12. The expression attribution and local differential calculation are correct; the page range is off by one. Checked https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.04051.

seams_checked.note: Checked the qft-mc01 page and its four items against the reconstruction's actual uses. F2 preserves positivity, normalization, Countable Choice, the quotient pairing, common invariant domain, adjoint restriction and closability. F3 preserves Cauchy–Schwarz including zero norms. F6 preserves state invariance and coefficient continuity; reconstruction step 2.3 supplies that continuity before invoking implementation. Neither side upgrades symmetric fields to self-adjoint closures or asserts generators from strong continuity.
